body: the `controller` only subscribes to the exact field name, if you want to watch nested value, use `useWatch`.
Isn't it counter intuitive that it works with controllers inside arrays but not inside the root object?

[From RHF docs on `setValue`](https://react-hook-form.com/api/useform/setvalue#main):
> Important: use replace from useFieldArray instead, update entire field array with setValue will be removed in the next major version.

You shouldn't use `setValue` with field arrays as you can encounter unwanted / weird behavior
On the use of `setValue` for field arrays deprecation you can read more in #7433 RHF next version discussion

I updated the codesandbox to use update instead of setValue for the array, and added a nested property for the array as well.
Again, it works fine for nested properties inside arrays.
https://codesandbox.io/s/react-hook-form-object-controlled-not-updated-qx4e2?file=/src/index.js

> So, the **not working** behavior is expect. In your case, you can
> 
>     * set your controlled input name as `nested` to track the whole object
> 
>     * use `setValue` with the exact or deeper nested field name
> 
> 
> ```js
> setValue("nested.objectControlled", {
>   nestedValue: "updated"
> });
> ```
> 
> or
> 
> ```js
> setValue("nested.objectControlled.nestedValue", "updated");
> ```
> 
> See [this CSB](https://codesandbox.io/s/react-hook-form-object-controlled-not-updated-forked-40e1c?file=/src/index.js) for example

That's indeed what I ended up doing in our code.
But I think that there is a small inconsistency to how it is handled with nested values inside arrays.
